report:
Reviewed the complete crates.sage_ir.crate.reexecution_and_invalidation claim, its single implementation association, and its complete single-test set. Both entries are explicitly TODO in sage_meta::todo, not ordinary implementation or executable behavioral evidence. The associated implementation comment acknowledges that selected interface backdating does not establish the complete guarantee. The associated test function is empty except for its TODO; it has no assertions and must not be counted as proving any incremental behavior.

The claim has four aspects: (1) distinguish producer reexecution from downstream invalidation, (2) permit cheap producer/keyed-lookup reexecution after coarse input changes, (3) require equal semantic results to backdate before expensive consumers, and (4) avoid promising zero upstream execution for every unrelated edit. The existing test TODO explicitly asks future edit tests to separately observe queries that reexecute, keyed-value equality/change, and downstream reuse across unchanged, relevant, and unrelated edits. This is an appropriate deferred evidence plan for all four aspects. Its prerequisite is completing and associating that multi-level edit evidence across the claimed semantic boundaries; observing only a selected interface or an overall result cannot establish the architecture-wide guarantee. A useful eventual assertion must allow upstream reexecution on coarse edits while rejecting expensive consumer execution when the keyed semantic result remains equal, and must separately check actual changed-result propagation.

The implementation TODO is accepted for its explicit limitation that selected interface backdating does not establish the complete guarantee. Its observation that unrelated same-file edits cause coarse reexecution is not itself a violation: the claim expressly permits that behavior. I do not treat that sentence as evidence of a bug or as a requirement to eliminate all upstream work. No general implementation completeness is asserted, and this review does not promote the selected-interface statement to verified production evidence. The documented gap remains deferred pending semantic-boundary implementation/evidence sufficient to show the equality barrier before expensive consumers. No ordinary implementation/test entries or N/A entries need separate adjudication.

Inspected captured source only, including the surrounding sage_ir model, maintaining-the-docs workflow, and review specification. Executed cargo meta review start with the captured coordinator instructions and cargo meta review read for those additional dependencies. No behavioral tests were executed, no passing placeholder is used as evidence, and no production or test source was modified. Accepting these explicit TODO entries preserves their TODO status; it does not certify the claimed behavior as implemented.
